passage:
Rain hammered the tin roof of the bus stop. Yamini had twenty minutes before the portfolio deadline at the design institute, and Vaibhav's folder was still in her bag; he had left it on her desk that morning. Her phone buzzed with a message from friends: "Anniversary pic?? 🎉" She thumbed it away and ran for the auto, holding the folder under her dupatta.

She reached the gate as he was pacing outside. He looked at the folder, then at her, and laughed with relief.

"If you get in, it means Ahmedabad for two years," she said, catching her breath. "I'll be sad. I'll also be proud. Let's figure out calls now, and tell each other honestly if it gets hard."

She posted nothing that day. He'd made the deadline; that felt like enough.

qa.q: Why was Yamini running through the rain?
qa.a: She was bringing Vaibhav the portfolio he had left on her desk, so he could submit it before the deadline at the institute.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling about the possible move to Ahmedabad?
qa.a: Mixed feelings: she says she will be sad but also proud, which shows she wants him to go without hiding her own side of it.

qa.q: What could Yamini and Vaibhav do if he does move for two years?
qa.a: Agree on realistic times for calls, keep telling each other honestly when it gets hard, and plan visits.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav see Yamini turning up at the gate with his folder?
qa.a: He probably feels backed by her, and reassured that his ambition is welcome and not something that threatens them.

grounding: Shows commitment expressed through reliability, honest talk and room for a partner's growth rather than a public post.

passage: First week of term. Tarun posted a photo of Vasudha with 'Mine forever' and a crown sticker. She laughed, but looked uneasy. When she said she'd joined a theatre group that rehearsed late, he sulked: 'You'll have no time for me.' Three weeks later. Vasudha's grandmother fell ill, and she had to go home to Mysore mid-semester. Tarun took her lab notes every day, typed them up, and called each night at nine as promised, even when she only wanted to cry. He stopped posting about them. It didn't feel like the point any more. Two months later. Vasudha was back, and on opening night he sat in the front row of her play with his roommate, clapping until his hands hurt. Afterwards he told her, 'I was scared the theatre thing meant losing you. It didn't. It's more you.' She squeezed his hand. 'You showed up every single day. That's what I'll remember.'

qa.q: What did Tarun post in the first week of term?
qa.a: A photo of Vasudha with 'Mine forever' and a crown sticker.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when Vasudha joined the theatre group?
qa.a: He felt insecure and afraid of losing her, which came out as sulking.

qa.q: How did Tarun's idea of love change over the weeks?
qa.a: From posting and possessiveness to reliability: daily notes, nightly calls and supporting her theatre.
That he showed up every single day when things were hard.

grounding: Shows a young man whose love shifts from possessive posts to reliability, honest talk and making room for his partner's growth.

passage: Raghav, you asked what love is, as if I keep a definition in the almirah. Listen instead. I married your Dadu at twenty, in Guwahati. Everyone thinks love is the wedding, the songs. For us it was the second year, when I wanted to finish my teaching degree and his mother said a daughter-in-law belongs in the kitchen. Your Dadu could have stayed quiet. Instead he sat with her and said, 'Binita will study. I'll cook on her exam days.' And he did, terrible dal and all, for two years. He never once showed me off to the neighbours. But he walked me to the exam hall every morning at seven. That's what I learned, Raghav. Love is who keeps showing up, and who makes room for you to grow. Not who shouts it loudest. Now go, phone your girl, and ask how her exam went.

qa.q: What did Dadu promise to do on Binita's exam days?
qa.a: Cook, even if the dal was terrible.

qa.q: What does Binita feel looking back on those two years?
qa.a: Binita feels grateful and deeply loved, remembering how Dadu kept showing up.

qa.q: What choice in Binita's story showed real commitment?
qa.a: Dadu backing Binita's teaching degree against his mother, then walking her to every exam.

qa.q: How did Dadu's mother seem to see Binita at first?
qa.a: As a daughter-in-law who belonged in the kitchen, not someone who should study.

grounding: An elder's story showing love as reliable support and room to grow, not as display or ownership.
